newsitem.title: USA: AmEx, other card companies post gains.
newsitem.headline: AmEx, other card companies post gains.

text.p: A rally in financial stocks Monday extended to the credit card speciality companies as well as American Express Co.
"Monoline" issuer MBNA Corp rose 1-3/8 to 31 and Advanta Corp jumped 1-1/4 to 22.
American Express Co, which conducted its annual shareholders meeting at the company headquarters in New York, advanced three to 64-1/8.
Although chairman and chief executive Harvey Golub did not spring any surprises at the American Express meeting, he gave a positive view of the charge and credit card business.

One shareholder got up to correct activist Evelyn Y. Davis's vague reference to the performance of the stock. The shareholder said he wanted to commend the American Express team because the stock price had jumped from 46-1/2 on the eve of the 1996 annual meeting to 61-1/8 last Friday.

In his formal remarks, Golub noted that in total return last year the American Express shares appreciated 40 percent while the gain was 23 percent for the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index and 35 percent for the S&P Financials.

Golub said that a key focus in 1996 was building up the card business. He said there are now franchise or network arrangements in 20 countries as the company executes its international strategy. He noted that revolving credit products have been launched in a number of markets.
Domestically, American Express has been rolling out co-branded cards, small business cards and stored valued cards.
"We continue to expand merchant acceptance," Golub said, adding that over 91 percent of card members' general spending can be accomodated on the American Express network.
The American Express Financial Advisors turned in record performance once more, Golub said.

Asked about the dividend policy, Golub said shareholders have the option of selling a portion of their shares if they want cash. A spokesman later told a reporter the company has viewed share repurchases as a better move than boosting the dividend, partly because of the tax effects.

Golub barely touched on a federal probe of competitive practices in the card industry, saying in answer to a question that the Department of Justice is considering the matter. American Express has been pushing the Visa and MasterCard card associations to let member banks have the option of issuing bank cards on the American Express network.

After American Express Co's first-quarter 1997 earnings announced last Thursday, analysts said the travel business was healthy with good credit quality. They also noted the strong American Express performance in financial advisors. In the quarter, net income rose 15 percent from a year ago to $454 million.
